headline: This is a behind-the-scenes tidy-up of how checkout charges cards. Payments should work exactly as before, so it is safe to ship.
what_changed: Customers will see no difference on the checkout page. They are charged the same amount, in US dollars, with the same order description.
The protection against charging a customer twice for the same order is still in place and works as it did before.
When the card payment company rejects a request, the error is now labelled more clearly. Developers can more easily tell payment failures apart from other problems.
The code that prepares each charge and its security details was split into smaller pieces. It does the same thing as before.
The saved change note says the payment code was moved into a new folder. No files were actually moved. The note slightly overstates the change, but nothing is broken.
questions_for_developer: The change note says the payment code moved into a new folder, but it did not move. Was that move planned and left out, or is the note just inaccurate?
good_news: The change is small and limited to the payment code. I checked the code that uses it, and nothing else depends on what changed.
The charge amount, currency and protection against double charges are all unchanged.
Failed orders are still marked as failed, just as before.
